title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: conclusion misses the point — believers consequently, not antecedently; Augustine
pass_a_gloss: Solution. Let us begin our response from the conclusion itself. We say therefore that that is not concluded which is posited in the controversy. For it is not asked whether election is only of those who will be believers, or, which comes to the same, of those whom God before the foundations of the world were laid foresees will believe; but whether that eternal act of the Divine election prerequires this foresight as a cause, or at least an antecedent condition: which we deny, and the adversaries can by no means prove. We concede to them that Election is only of believers; but not of believers in the Divine foresight antecedently to the election itself, but of believers in the Divine foresight consequently, and by virtue of the grace prepared and destined for them in the election, according to that of Augustine On the Predestination of the Saints chapter 18, Therefore we were going to be such because he himself chose that we should be such through grace. And chapter 10. By predestination God foresaw what he himself was going to do. He has like things in chapter 17. Which places of Augustine if anyone consults, he will find both the best solution of this Arminian argument, and the best explanation of this Pauline context.
pass_b_english: Sol. Start from their conclusion: it does not settle what is in controversy. The question is not whether election is only of those who will be believers — or of those God foresaw before the world's foundations would believe — but whether that eternal act of divine election prerequires that foresight as cause, or at least antecedent condition. We deny it; adversaries cannot prove it. We grant election is of believers only — not believers in divine foresight before election, but believers consequently, by virtue of the grace prepared and destined for them in election. So Augustine, De praed. Sanct. 18: we were going to be such because he chose that we should be such through grace; and ch. 10: by predestination God foresaw what he himself would do (likewise ch. 17). Consult those places for the best solution of this Arminian argument and the best reading of this Pauline context.
source_text: Sol. Ab ipsa conclusione ordiamur responsionem nostram. Dicimus ergo, non concludi illud quod positum est in controversia. Non enim quaeritur utrum electio sit solummodo eorum qui credentes sunt futuri, vel, quod eodem recidit, eorum quos Deus ante jacta mundi fundamenta praevidet credituros; sed utrum aeternus ille actus electionis Divinae praerequirat hanc praevisionem tanquam causam, aut saltem conditionem antecedaneam: quod nos negamus, et adversarii neutiquam possunt probare. Concedimus illis, Electionem esse tantum credentium; sed non credentium in praescientia Divina antecedenter ad ipsam electionem, sed credentium in praescientia Divina consequenter, et virtute gratiae in electione illis praeparatae et destinatae, juxta illud Augustini De Praed. Sanct. cap. 18, Ideo tales eramus futuri quia elegit ipse ut tales per gratiam essemus. Et cap. 10. Praedestinatione Deus praescivit quid fuerat ipse facturus. Consimilia habet cap. 17. Quae loca Augustini si quis consulat, et Arminiani hujus argumenti optimam solutionem, et Paulini hujus contextus optimam explicationem inveniet.
